lesson.title: Part to part, part to whole
lesson.body: A class of 12 boys and 18 girls has boys to girls 12 : 18 (part to part) and girls to all pupils 18 : 30 (part to whole).

lesson.title: Order matters
lesson.body: Boys to girls is 12 : 18; girls to boys is 18 : 12. Write the terms in the order the words say.

lesson.title: Multiply or divide both
lesson.body: Equivalent ratios multiply or divide both terms by the same number: 2 : 3 = 4 : 6 = 8 : 12. Adding the same number does not keep a ratio.

lesson.title: Simplest form
lesson.body: A ratio is in simplest form when its terms share no factor but 1: divide both by their GCF. 12 : 18 = 2 : 3.

lesson.title: Find one part
lesson.body: To share ₱60 in the ratio 2 : 3, add the parts: 5. One part is ₱60 ÷ 5 = ₱12, so the shares are ₱24 and ₱36.

lesson.title: How many times
lesson.body: How many times larger is 24 than 6? Divide: 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Taking away, 24 − 6 = 18, says how much larger, not how many times.

lesson.title: In proportion
lesson.body: Two quantities are in proportion when they grow by the same times: 3 cups for 4 servings, 6 cups for 8 servings, 9 cups for 12.

lesson.title: Find one first
lesson.body: When the numbers do not divide neatly, find the cost of one, then multiply: 4 notebooks for ₱60 is ₱15 each, so 7 cost ₱105.

formats.prompt: A class has {b} boys and {g} girls. Complete the ratio of girls to all the pupils: {g} : ?
A basket has {b} mangoes and {g} bananas. Complete the ratio of bananas to all the fruit: {g} : ?

hints: The second part of this ratio is the whole, not the other part.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the other part. This ratio compares {g} with the whole, {b} + {g}.
{value} is the part already given. The second term is the whole.

templates.construct: Write a part-to-part ratio from a part and the whole

formats.prompt: There are {t} pupils in a class, and {b} are boys. Complete the ratio of boys to girls: {b} : ?
A tray holds {t} eggs, and {b} are brown. The rest are white. Complete the ratio of brown eggs to white eggs: {b} : ?

hints: This ratio compares two parts: find the other part first.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the whole. This ratio compares {b} with the other part, {t} − {b}.
{value} is {t} + {b}. Take {b} away from {t} to find the other part.

templates.construct: Express one quantity as a fraction of the whole from a ratio

formats.prompt: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is {x} : {y}. What fraction of the class are boys?
A drink is made of juice and water in the ratio {x} : {y}. What fraction of the drink is juice?

hints: A ratio of {x} : {y} means {x} part{x == 1 ? '' : 's'} and {y} part{y == 1 ? '' : 's'}.
There are {x} + {y} = {x + y} parts in all.
{x} part{x == 1 ? '' : 's'} out of {x + y}: write it as a fraction.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} compares {x} with {y}. A fraction of the whole is {x} out of {x} + {y}.
{frac(value)} is the other part's share. The question asks for the first part.

templates.construct: Write a ratio in simplest form

formats.prompt: Write {a} : {b} in simplest form: {x} : ?

hints: Divide both terms by the same number until they share no factor.
{a} and {b} can both be divided by {g}.

distractors.feedback: {value} takes the same amount from both terms. Divide both by {g} instead.
{value} leaves {b} as it was. Divide it by {g} too.

templates.construct: Find the missing term of an equivalent ratio

formats.prompt: Find the missing number so the ratios are equivalent: {x} : {y} = {x * k} : ?

hints: Equivalent ratios multiply both terms by the same number.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds {x * k - x} to {y}. Equivalent ratios multiply both terms: × {k}.
{value} adds {y} to {x * k}. Multiply {y} by {k}.

formats.prompt: 1 bag holds {u} kg of rice, 2 bags hold {2 * u} kg and 3 bags hold {3 * u} kg. How many kilograms do {m} bags hold?
A ratio table: 1 pack has {u} pencils, 2 packs have {2 * u}, 3 packs have {3 * u}. How many pencils are in {m} packs?

hints: Each extra bag or pack adds the same amount.
templates.explain: The table goes up by {u} each time: {m} × {u} = {answer}.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds 1 for each step. Each step adds {u}.
{value} is the next number in the table, for 4. The question asks for {m}.

templates.construct: Share an amount in a given ratio

formats.prompt: Ana and Ben share ₱{total} in the ratio {x} : {y}. How much does Ana get?
{total} mangoes are shared between two families in the ratio {x} : {y}. How many does the first family get?

hints: Add the parts of the ratio to find how many equal parts there are.
{x} + {y} = {x + y} parts, and {total} ÷ {x + y} = {p} for each part.

distractors.feedback: {value} shares equally. In the ratio {x} : {y}, the first share is {x} part{x == 1 ? '' : 's'} out of {x + y}.
{value} is one part. The first share is {x} part{x == 1 ? '' : 's'}.
{value} is the other share, {y} part{y == 1 ? '' : 's'}. The question asks for the first.

templates.construct: Find a quantity from a ratio and the other quantity

formats.prompt: The ratio of boys to girls is {x} : {y}. There are {girls} girls. How many boys are there?
In a pet shop the ratio of cats to dogs is {x} : {y}. There are {girls} dogs. How many cats are there?

hints: Find what one part of the ratio stands for.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds the same as the ratio's terms differ by. Find one part first: {girls} ÷ {y} = {p}.
{value} is one part. The answer is {x} part{x == 1 ? '' : 's'}.

templates.construct: Find how many times larger one quantity is than another

formats.prompt: A mango costs ₱{big} and a calamansi costs ₱{s}. How many times as much does the mango cost?
A tree is {big} m tall and a fence is {s} m tall. How many times as tall as the fence is the tree?

hints: How many times larger means divide, not take away.
steps: So it is {answer} times as large

distractors.feedback: {value} is how much more, {big} − {s}. How many times larger means {big} ÷ {s}.
{value} is {big} + {s}. How many times larger means {big} ÷ {s}.

formats.prompt: A recipe uses {f} cups of flour for {s} servings. How many cups of flour are needed for {s * k} servings?
{f} cups of rice feed {s} people. How many cups feed {s * k} people?

hints: Find how many times bigger the new amount is.
{s * k} ÷ {s} = {k}, so everything is {k} times as much.
templates.explain: {k} times the servings needs {k} times the flour: {f} × {k} = {answer}.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds {s * k - s}, as the servings went up. In proportion, multiply: × {k}.
{value} multiplies {f} by {s * k}. The servings went up {k} times, so multiply {f} by {k}.

templates.construct: Use a unit price to find the cost of a different quantity

formats.prompt: {n} pencils cost ₱{c}. At the same price, how much do {m} pencils cost?
{n} eggs cost ₱{c}. How much do {m} eggs cost at the same price?

hints: Find the price of one first.

distractors.feedback: {value} is ₱{c} × {m}. ₱{c} buys {n}: find the price of one first.
{value} {m > n ? 'adds' : 'takes away'} {abs(m - n)}, as the number bought changed. In proportion, find the price of one and multiply.

formats.prompt: On a map, 1 cm stands for {s} km. Two towns are {d} cm apart on the map. How many kilometres apart are they?
A map's scale is 1 cm to {s} km. A road is {d} cm long on the map. How long is the real road, in kilometres?

hints: Every centimetre on the map is {s} km.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds {d} to {s}. Each centimetre is {s} km: multiply.
{value} km is one centimetre. The towns are {d} cm apart.
